sections.content: How many people are "events managers and organisers"?

48,010 people

were counted on the census as "events managers and organisers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Events managers and organisers co-ordinate business conferences, exhibitions, concerts and similar events.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "events managers and organisers", 19.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "events managers and organisers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "events managers and organisers" included:

  • pharmacists
  • design occupations (other)
  • finance and investment analysts and advisers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "events managers and organisers" there were more women than men (68.1% compared with 31.9%).

This means "events managers and organisers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 31.9% and women made up 68.1% of "events managers and organisers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "events managers and organisers" included:

  • merchandisers
  • launderers, dry cleaners and pressers
  • air travel assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "events managers and organisers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "events managers and organisers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "events managers and organisers", 8.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (66.7% compared with 33.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (80.5%) than self-employed (19.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wandsworth, this is in the same region of London.
